question: At exactly identical posthistory population mean of reproductive assurance, how does shrinking the transmitted diploid assurance-locus dispersion affect immediate payoff and finite persistence, with/without new postshock mutation?
genetic_intervention: For each of the eight recipient assurance allele copies pairs at time400, write A_new = mean(A_original) + q*(A_original - mean(A_original)) for q=0,.5,1. Mean is preserved exactly (floating arithmetic tol 1e-12). Variance becomes q^2 times original. Other loci, allele_origin, mutation flags and individual IDs are unchanged. q=1 bitwise identity. Genetic covariance of assurance with matching/investment also scales q, so this is NOT a pure variance intervention.
randomization: All q and mutation treatments within setting/history/background/postvisitor/budget/repeat receive same deterministic postshock RNG streams; the post mutation mask keeps assurance mutable when rate 0.01 and disables all mutation when rate 0.0.
descriptive_primary: For each setting and recipient background separately, report q=0 minus q=1 occupancy averaged over all four histories, both post visitor environments, both budgets and four postshock random streams, for mutation 0 and 0.01 separately. Also report q=.5. No pass/fail threshold or post-hoc omission.
readouts: A mean and allele variance at switch
initial maternal viable output per resident
t80 A genotype variance conditional on survival
boundaries: This is an exploratory *post-outcome* test on four exposed historical visitor seeds; no independent generality.
q=0 destroys assurance standing variance but also removes its linkage/cross-locus genotype covariance; effects cannot uniquely be attributed to variance.
Post-mutation 0 also freezes new variants at all three loci, not only assurance; distinguish from actual assurance-locus isolation.
Outcome-informed bottleneck (N=8), budget 3/4 are not calibrated natural-island levels.
This is an inherited-state intervention, not a manipulation of realized evolutionary-order timing.
Do not relabel the previously failed independent16 donor-transfer gate or mutational-priority gate.
